hints.title: Create the copies first
hints.body: You cannot connect a back-reference until the target copy exists. First create one new node for every original node.

hints.title: Remember the mapping
hints.body: A hash map from an original node to its copy lets you translate any reference, whether it points forward or backward.

hints.title: Connect both kinds of links
hints.body: For each original node, set the copy's `next` to the copy of the original's next node, and set the copy's back-reference to the copy of the original's target.

hints.title: Pseudocode
hints.body:
```
if values is empty: return []
originals = one new node per value, linked in order
copies = one new node per value, linked in order
map = empty dictionary
for each index: map[originals[index]] = copies[index]
for each index:
    if random[index] is not -1:
        originals[index].random = originals[random[index]]
        copies[index].random = copies[random[index]]
output = []
walk the copies in order:
    find the index of node.random in copies
    append [node.value, index or -1]
return output
```

This is pseudocode, not a complete solution.
